title: GAP Coverage: Toyota Collects Unearned Millions Each Year by Charging Early Contract Payoff Fees, Lawsuit Says
summary: A class-action complaint alleges Toyota Motor Credit keeps unearned GAP waiver fees when customers pay off their loans early instead of refunding them.

assertions.quote: Toyota knowingly collects and keeps tens of millions of dollars in unearned fees from its customers each year

verdicts.note: The subject of multiple real class-action lawsuits against lenders, though allegations rather than a settled, universal finding.

CFPB examiners found servicers failed, across every state, to ensure refunds of the unearned portion of GAP and service-contract premiums when a loan terminated early via payoff, repossession, or total loss.

CFPB examiners found servicers failed to request or apply refunds of the unearned, financed portion of GAP product fees after a vehicle was repossessed and the GAP contract canceled, instead folding the unrefunded GAP cost into inflated deficiency balances sent to debt buyers; the report generalizes the underlying rule to any case where 'the loan otherwise ends early'.

assertions.quote: Toyota is required to 'waive' the $2,000 difference
